Implement 3 final residual fixes in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (and migrate-detect.ts where noted) — the Nxeon migration engine. After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN (exit 0) and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` (green). Do NOT run the worker, deploy, or commit. Read the relevant regions first. Report per-fix final line numbers. Refuse-and-name when unsure.

## FIX STD-1 — standalone container: capture + reproduce (or honestly refuse) HostConfig knobs
This ONLY affects the STANDALONE (non-compose) container path (compose containers get these natively via `up`). Read the container inspect template (search `netmode`, `runuser`, `workdir`, `privileged`, `devices`, `CapAdd`, the Go-template block ~1020-1044), its parser (~1240-1290), `SrcContainer` type, `planContainer` + `buildRunCommand` (~1775-1878), and the existing REFUSE list (devices>0, custom cmd/entrypoint, `container:` netmode, >1 custom network).
Today the template captures only name/image/state/restart/netmode/runuser/workdir/privileged/device-count/CapAdd/cmd/entrypoint. Everything else on HostConfig is dropped, so a standalone container is recreated with DIFFERENT (often MORE privileged) settings, silently. 
- CAPTURE + REPRODUCE (add to template, parser, SrcContainer type, and emit in buildRunCommand): `CapDrop` (→ `--cap-drop`), `Sysctls` (→ `--sysctl k=v`), `Ulimits` (→ `--ulimit name=soft:hard`), `Dns` (→ `--dns`), `ExtraHosts` (→ `--add-host`), `Tmpfs` (→ `--tmpfs`), `ReadonlyRootfs` (→ `--read-only`), `SecurityOpt` (→ `--security-opt`). Mirror how CapAdd is already templated/parsed/emitted. Validate every value before it reaches the command (allowlist chars; drop anything unparseable rather than shell-injecting). Cap list sizes sensibly.
- REFUSE (add to the existing refuse list, do NOT silently reproduce): GPU (`--gpus`/`runtime=nvidia` — depends on target hardware), `pid`/`ipc` mode referencing another container or host (`pid: host`, `pid: container:*`, `ipc: host`), and any HostConfig field you capture but can't safely reproduce. For a refused container, push a `copied`-status step naming exactly which feature made it unsafe to auto-recreate and how to run it by hand — mirror the existing standalone refuse style.
Keep the Go template robust: guard every `{{range}}`/field with `{{if}}` so a missing field never aborts the whole template (the existing `devices` comment explains this failure mode — follow it).

## FIX A7 — gRPC upstreams: proxy correctly or honestly refuse
The nginx vhost builder uses `proxy_pass http://` + `proxy_http_version 1.1` for proxied apps; gRPC needs `grpc_pass grpc://` over HTTP/2. Detect a gRPC hint for a proxied vhost — the source nginx config used `grpc_pass` for that server, OR the app is known-gRPC (hard in general). When the SOURCE vhost used `grpc_pass` (grep the source nginx dump the engine already keeps), reproduce it as `grpc_pass grpc://127.0.0.1:<port>;` with `http2` on the listen, instead of a plain `proxy_pass`. If you can't reliably tell, do NOT guess — leave the normal proxy_pass but, when the source config contained `grpc_pass`, push an honest step naming that the site uses gRPC and the generated config proxies it as HTTP/1.1 (may not work) — reference the kept source config. Only touch the proxied-app vhost case.

## FIX SCALE-CAP — name truncations instead of silently dropping
The engine caps several scans (search `head -n 40` containers, `head -n 120` images, `head -n 4000` for `nginx -T`, `slice(0, 20)`/`slice(0,40)` app dirs, `MAX_*` consts, `head -n 60` homes, `head -n 80` mysql.user/server_name). When a cap is actually HIT (the source had MORE than the cap), the extra items are silently dropped and the run looks complete. Fix: where a cap is applied to a source enumeration, detect when the raw count exceeded the cap and surface ONE honest note per capped category (e.g. "your old server has 63 containers; the 40 largest/first were inventoried — N were not migrated, list them with `docker ps -a`"). Do this for the high-impact caps at least: containers, images, app dirs, domains/vhosts, and the `nginx -T` 4000-line truncation. Prefer capturing the true count cheaply (many scan scripts already emit an authoritative count like CCOUNT — reuse those; search `CCOUNT`) and comparing. Don't change the caps themselves; just stop the silence.

## Constraints
- Reuse existing helpers/validators; match the single-quoted `sh -c '…'` style and the Go-template guarding pattern; validate every interpolated value.
- Do NOT regress any container/compose/data-safety/web/units work already in the file (commit 9c91212).
- Finish only when tsc is clean AND the consolidate test passes. Report per-fix final line numbers, the full list of HostConfig fields you added (captured vs refused), and which caps you added a note for.
